name: Jorōgumo
description: The Jorōgumo is a spider yōkai of Japanese folklore, traditionally said to be a Trichonephila clavata that has lived for centuries and gained the power to take the form of a beautiful woman, luring men to ensnare and devour. Famous as the haunt of Jōren Falls in the Izu Peninsula.

aliases.name: 女郎蜘蛛
aliases.meaning: 'Whore spider' or 'woman spider', the entomological / vernacular spelling

aliases.name: Jorō spider
aliases.meaning: Trichonephila clavata, the golden silk orb-weaver — the real spider lending its name to the yokai

origin: Native to Japanese folklore, with regional legends concentrated in central and western Honshu, especially the Izu Peninsula (Shizuoka), Kashikobuchi (Sendai, Miyagi), and the mountain forests of Kyoto and Kii.
